::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Allow only certain commands in own environment](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/136260/allow-only-certain-commands-in-own-environment), asked by [user26756](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/37615/user26756) on TeX Stack Exchange (2013-10-03; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I would like to define an environment `myenv` and allow only certain predefined commands to be executed betwwen `\begin{myenv}` and `\end{myenv}`. 
>
> For example I want text typed there to be ignored and also to give a list of commands which are allowed. Is there a way to achieve this?
>
> Thanks.
:::

For ignoring text, you could use `myenv` as a special type of `comment` environment (from the [package of the same name](http://ctan.org/pkg/comment)).  I don't think there's a way to only allow a certain number of macros, however.  You can disallow any macro by redefining it to give an error message.

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{comment}
\usepackage{lipsum}

\newcommand{\foo}{bar}

\specialcomment{myenv}{
	\newcommand{\nomacros}{%
		\GenericError{}{%
			Illegal macro%
		}{}{
		This macro is not allowed within the `myenv' environment
		}}%
	\let\foo\nomacros
	\let\bar\nomacros
}{}


\begin{document}

\lipsum[1]

\begin{myenv}
\lipsum[1]
\foo\bar
\end{myenv}

\end{document}
```

The console will give:

>     ! Illegal macro.
>     
>     
>     Type  H <return>  for immediate help.
>      ...                                              
>                                                       
>     l.2 \foo
>             \bar
>     ? h
>      This macro is not allowed within the `myenv' environment 
>     ? 
>     
>     ! Illegal macro.
>     
>     
>     Type  H <return>  for immediate help.
>      ...                                              
>                                                       
>     l.2 \foo\bar
>                 
>     ? x
>     No pages of output.
